title: Monthly Wholesale Trade benchmark revision — sales, inventories and I/S ratios restated on the 2023 and 2024 Annual Integrated Economic Survey
source: EST: TWO Census primaries fetched direct 2026-09-06 by this event's own initial research. (1) census.gov/wholesale/index.html (HTTP 200, 527,648 bytes), announcements block, verbatim: "Intention to Revise - Monthly Wholesale sales, inventories, and inventories/sales ratios estimates are anticipated to be revised based on historical corrections and the results of the 2023 and 2024 Annual Integrated Economic Survey. Revised not adjusted estimates and corresponding adjusted estimates are tentatively scheduled for release on October 26, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. EDT." (2) census.gov/mtis/index.html (HTTP 200, 683,571 bytes), which carries the retail and wholesale halves in one sentence and dates them separately: "...tentatively scheduled for release on September 28, 2026 and October 26, 2026, respectively." Upstream input corroborated: the 2024 AIES estimates published 2026-09-03 and the 2023 AIES main release 2026-02-26 (census.gov/programs-surveys/aies.html, same-day fetch), so both survey vintages this revision consumes already exist. Stays estimate on three counts: Census's own word is "tentatively", the lane may not self-confirm an in-sweep discovery, and the date is ABSENT from census.gov/economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html (179 rows parsed; October 2026 runs 10-20 then 10-27). Checked 2026-09-06
notes: DISCOVERED by the wholesale-trade-2026-12-09 adjacency sweep (proposals/mwts-benchmark-revision-2026-10-26.from-wholesale-trade-2026-12-09.json, now shadowed by this file); this canonical entry is written by the event's own initial research, which read that proposal first and both confirms and sharpens it. What the restatement is: the entire published history of Monthly Wholesale Trade — sales, inventories and the inventories/sales ratio, adjusted and not — re-benchmarked on two Annual Integrated Economic Survey vintages at once. Measured this session from 159 monthly + 96 daily ALFRED vintages of WHLSLRIRSA/WHLSLRSMSA/WHLSLRIMSA (1992-01 to 2026-06, 414 observations): this series has been benchmark-revised on exactly 12 dates since ALFRED's archive opens — 2014-04-14, 2015-04-14, 2016-04-13, 2017-04-14, 2018-06-14, 2019-04-18, 2020-04-15, 2021-04-15, 2022-04-14, 2023-04-14, 2024-04-15, 2025-04-16 — and on all 12 the revision was BUNDLED into a regular monthly release (a new reference month was added the same day). 2026 broke that 12-year cadence: between the 2026-03-28 and 2026-09-06 vintages only 5 recent months moved, none by more than 0.01, so no spring benchmark happened. 2026-10-26 is the deferred one, it carries two AIES years rather than one, and it is the FIRST STANDALONE benchmark revision in the archive — no monthly report, no GDPNow vintage (the Atlanta Fed's PostedUpdates sheet runs 10-20 then 10-27). Typical magnitude, measured on months at least 15 months old so ordinary monthly revisions are excluded: every one of the 12 restated 126+ historical months of inventories (median 172, back to 2000-2013) at a median 0.126% per month and a median worst month of 1.034%; the two outliers (2015, 2021) reached 3-4%. On the 2-decimal ratio, 640 month-level changes give P(move >= 0.02) = 23.0% and P(>= 0.03) = 4.2%. Impact stays LOW and symbols empty: no house playbook is macro-keyed (re-run grep of trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md, 0 hits, 2026-09-06), no instrument attaches, and a benchmark revision has no consensus forecast to surprise against — it restates the past rather than reporting the present. Two reading cautions belong with the entry. Its only live channel is the corridor: 10-26 sits two days before advance-economic-indicators-2026-10-28, which is GDPNow's FINAL 2026:Q3 nowcast, and three days before gdp-q3-2026-advance-2026-10-29 — whether the 10-28 advance report carries September wholesale inventories on the restated basis is not stated by Census and is the open question. And the schedule risk is real rather than formal: the same MTIS announcement carries a Special Notice that M3 revised historical data and seasonal adjustment models "will remain unchanged for the remainder of 2026" due to "schedule and resource constraints", and this series has already skipped one benchmark this year. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
